items.title: Skill prices are in the old currency (Attack = 2)
items.body: BUDGET2 moved the stats to 3A + H and fitted N (x 1.13) with skill prices unchanged. The prices were measured in 2A + H points: RECOST1's yardstick valued a point at 4.17 win-rate points (+1 Attack 9.5, +1 Health 3.0); a 3A + H point is (9.5 + 3.0) / 4 = 3.1, so in the new currency a measured price would be about x1.33. The canon check (tools/skill_canon_2026_10_31.js, 200 paired fights on 6 vanilla carriers) reads more: a point of skill price buys about 2.2 points of stats (kappa 0.46 [0.38, 0.58]). Cheap skills next to stats make cards with skills stronger than vanilla cards of the same budget. docs/balance/budget2-2026-10-31.md sections 5 and 6.
options: Scale every measured price x1.33 and re-fit (a second full re-fit, N re-fitted)
Re-measure the skills against the re-canonised anchors (BUDGET2-2) and re-fit then
items.default: Re-measure the skills against the re-canonised anchors (BUDGET2-2) and re-fit then
items.outcome: Coordinator (owner's standing 'fill in the decisions'): re-measure every skill price against the anchors (after BUDGET2-2), in package SKILL2. No blanket x1.33.

items.title: Re-canonise the anchor skills from one shared measure?
items.body: X14: 12 canon anchors (15 points) are marked in canonical/skill-costs.json (canon: true): Armor 1/2, Poison 1/2, Bleed 1/2, Regen 2, Pounce 2, Quick, Sweep 2, Fork, Rage, Inspiring 1, Gold on Ready 1, Shell 2. On one shared set of carriers their RECOST1 prices disagree: 13 of 15 fall outside the interval the other anchors give them (Sweep 2 reads 2.9 vs price 1.1, Fork 3.0 vs 1.27, Gold on Ready 3.1 vs 2.31, Rage 2.0 vs 0.99; Armor 2 2.1 vs 4.53, Poison 1 1.2 vs 3.0). RECOST1 measured each on its own carriers. A canon is only a yardstick if its prices come from one measure.
options: Re-canonise: each anchor's canon price = its worth in this shared measure at 400 fights, scaled so the anchors' total stays
Keep the RECOST1 prices as canon; read the tool's results as relative only
Shrink the canon to the anchors that agree (Pounce 2, Quick) and add others
items.default: Re-canonise: each anchor's canon price = its worth in this shared measure at 400 fights, scaled so the anchors' total stays
items.outcome: Coordinator (owner's standing 'fill in the decisions'): yes, re-set the anchors' prices from one shared measurement first (SKILL2).

items.title: Raid win-rate targets: warm-ups 60%, the Core 40%
items.body: RAIDBAL1 (docs/balance/raidbal1-2026-10-30.md) needed a target for the Goliath's fights and the evaluation protocol has none for raids. Proposed and tuned to: each warm-up (Left Tentacle, Right Tentacle, Tail) about 60% (green 52-68%), the Core about 40% (green 32-48%, the protocol's boss band). A win is the part's bramble destroyed within the 20 turns. Measured on a fresh part against three Map 13 decks (the Raid Banner's map) at +2 levels (owner W8): the Map reference, Reference-2 and the deck optimizer's Map 13 optimum, 40 fights a deck. Result: warm-ups 58-62%, the Core 40% (47% on fresh seeds). At the unlock level itself (+0): warm-ups about 53%, the Core 34%. project-state.md still says 'raid bosses sit near 20%' (RW2-4); that line predates this per-fight measure.
items.outcome: Owner 2026-10-30 23:25: "The rest of the decisions seem okay." Default: warm-ups 60%, the Core 40%.

items.title: Your deck matters little in a raid fight
items.body: The boss's cards fight at 20% Attack / 15% Health (tuning), so on the warm-ups the two CPU allies and you clear its board by about turn 6-10 and then race its bramble; the three reference decks land within about 35 points of each other, and +2 levels moves a fight only 2-11 points. RAIDBAL1 therefore tuned with the brambles (and +60 raider bramble, which only the Core feels: the raiders never lose bramble on the warm-ups). Raising the boss's card strength makes the warm-ups real fights but crushes the Core (its stumps and Beak Strike), and the stumps are shared with the classic trench. A per-part boss strength (a part-level tuning field read by buildRaidFullFight) would let both be tuned; that is a code change for another package.

items.outcome: Owner 2026-10-30 23:25: default. Keep the bramble-led tuning.

items.title: The CPU now saves for its big cards: keep it at this strength?
items.body: Your X24 note: the CPU now holds its Lumber for a card worth 1.5x its best paying play (within 3 pitches, at most 2 turns held back, never while losing badly). Measured on Maps 0-20 (335 fights, 12 games each, the new-player reference decks): the CPU played 19.5% of the cost 3+ cards it drew before, 27.5% after (cost 2+: 22.4% -> 33.1%); the player's win rate went 52.6% -> 54.3%. A stricter version (1.25x bar, pitching the best play whatever the gap) played the same number of big cards and cost the CPU about 3 more points. Options: (a) keep it, retune those decks in the next balance pass; (b) keep it and drop the weakest cost 3+ cards from skirmish decks (your 'then we shouldn't have included it in the deck'); (c) undo it.

items.title: A row each, one shared bramble, allied slots both ways
items.body: Built as the raid's model: player 1 (the host) holds the front row, player 2 the middle row; each plays from their own hand, deck and Lumber, one play a turn as in a normal fight; each leader opens in the centre of its row. The party has ONE bramble: every player's bramble Health added up and their passives merged (the raid's mergeRaidCastles). Either player may also play into the other's empty slots (K12); the unit stays its player's and holds that row. A unit in the middle row strikes from there (as a raid ally's), it never steps up into the front.

items.title: The race window: 120 ms
items.body: K12's rule ("If there's ever a race condition, smaller index player takes priority"): every placement is a claim to the room's host; the host gathers the claims that arrive within 120 ms of the first one as one moment and lands them lower player index first, each checked against the board as it stands, so of two claims on one slot player 1's lands and player 2's card goes back to its hand with a note naming who took it. A claim on a slot that already landed is refused whoever made it (no stealing a slot after it shows). A longer window favours player 1 more often; a shorter one follows arrival order more closely.

items.title: CPU allies play first: alongside you, or before you may play?
items.body: W4 ("The allies should play their cards first if CPU btw, taking a random amount of time between 0.5 to 3.0s. (0.5 to 1.5s in the first turn only)"). Built: each CPU ally starts its own timer as the turn begins (0.5-1.5 s on a floor's first turn, 0.5-3.0 s after) and plays when it fires; you may play at the same time, and the round waits for every CPU ally. So if you wait a moment you see its play first; if you are quick you go first. The other reading would lock your hand until every CPU ally has played (up to 3 s each turn).

items.title: "Adjacent" includes the card in front of or behind yours
items.body: W10 ("You can also place cards in your allies' rows and vice versa if you have a card adjacent. However you cannot use your allies' 'network' to place cards."). Built: a slot is open to you when one of YOUR cards is beside it in its row, or in the same column one row in front or behind (that is how a card of yours can be next to an ally's row at all), plus your own row's centre. An ally's cards open nothing for you. Units a skill makes count as the player's whose row they stand in.

items.title: Nothing on the board and your centre taken: the slots beside it open
items.body: With W10's rule an ally (or a CPU ally) who plays into the centre of YOUR row while you have no card on the board would shut you out of the fight. Built: in that case the two slots beside your row's centre are open to you (the normal game's empty-board rule, legalSlots). Otherwise your row's centre is always open to you when it is free.

items.title: Equipment hardiness: Lives on top of durability (Hardy N), and the anti-equipment skills Sunder and Dismantle
items.body: Your 23:58 on OWN-Q2: "Equipment can be destroyed through specific anti-equipment skill. But only at 50% chance ... maybe with armor 'lives' default 1, some have 2-3." Proposal (docs/proposals-2026-10-26.md section 1): durability stays as the wear counter (hit 1, acid 2, Corrode 2; EQ2). New: Lives N (keyword Hardy N, default 1 = today's rule). A break takes one life: durability reaching 0 (then it refills) or a break skill succeeding; at 0 lives the piece is destroyed. Dragonscale Mail Hardy 2; Hardy 3 for a few named Legendary+ metal pieces. Sunder (On Hit: 50% to break the target's piece, 1.0), Dismantle (On Play: 50% to break the facing enemy's piece or a loose one, 0.5), Pulverise breaks a life for sure (+0.5 in its price). Tamper-proof blocks stealing only. A dropped piece keeps lives and wear; the next unit picks it up after Equip Time. Price: equipLifeMult = min(D x L, 4) / 4 + 0.35 for a 2nd life + 0.2 for a 3rd. Shown as gold rings above the durability pips and a gem badge on the card. Also to settle: does Pulverise break for sure or roll 50%?
options: A. Lives on top of durability (recommended)
B. Lives replace durability (only break skills, acid and Corrode take lives, 50% each)
C. Hardy as a quality: immune to break skills, half wear; no lives
items.default: A. Lives on top of durability (recommended)

items.title: Should a PvP stranger's deck be levelled to your battle rating?
items.body: Your G22 question, from the code: PvP is not scaled to your BR. The opponent is a recorded deck (a player's or a seeded stranger) from your Elo tier (6 tiers on the rating curve, widening one tier at a time until at least 6 candidates), drawn at random with a 60% pull toward decks whose battle rating is near yours (weight 0.4 + 0.6 x e^(-|BR difference| / max(8, your BR / 4))). Its cards fight as recorded; nothing is levelled up or down, and the win moves your rating by Elo (K 24). items.title: The CPU is stronger on Maps 0-20: retune the road after EN8?
items.body: Measured (tools/en8_cpu_pitch_2026_10_24.js, every fight of Maps 0-20 and their side maps as the game builds it, 40 games each, the reference player at Smart): the new-player win rate fell from 76.0% to 64.4% (docs/balance/en8-cpu-pitch-before-all.json -> -after-all.json). Of the ~12 points: the CPU's new pitch about 5.5 (its first card down: round 1.19 -> 1.01 on average; the owner's 4-of-20 case 2.59 -> 1.54), brambles that heal an ally instead of themselves (castleRegen, P24-17) about 3.7 (probe files -nopitch / -nopitch-regen), the lethal guard about 0.6 (-after-noguard), the rest (Rampart's columns, Guardian vs Thorns, Windfall) about 2. Nothing was retuned here. Proposal: the next BAL / road-curve pass re-measures and re-tunes the outliers (tools/skirmish_pass.js curve). PRO3 (2026-10-25) did that pass by the agreed schedule (roadCurveTarget, green = target +/- 8): every fight of Maps 0-20 and their side maps measured (tools/skirmish_pass.js measure, 40 games, 241 fights), then CPU deck swaps only (a card of the map's pool for another, the leader, first-clear card and deck size kept, no Shield or Health change). On the curve: green 68 -> 117, too easy 77 -> 56, too hard 81 -> 53; main-map mean 64.0% -> 67.2% (131 decks changed). items.title: Stone/Metal versions of the lumber gatherers, and other ways to make Lumber: which to build?

Other Lumber sources: Felling (On Kill: +1 Lumber), Salvage (when one of your Structures dies: +2 Lumber), Windfall field (after a Storm round, both sides +1 Lumber), Scavenger (when an ally dies: +1 Lumber), Coppice (a tree Structure that gives +1 Lumber each round while undamaged), Driftwood tide (at Ebb, +1 Lumber on beach maps).

Caves & Alcoves is the Stone map: its Quarry Mole (Bedrock: Armor while you hold 2+ Stone) and Dynamite Packrat (costs 1 Stone) are there to spend it. Stone counts 2 points to Lumber's 1 in the game's resource worth, so Quarry's 1 : 1 is a profit, which is why a card with it pays 2.5 budget points. The alternative you sketched, "at round end spend 2 Lumber -> 1 Stone", is a new skill (a small engine change) and a loss in points; worth it only if Stone should be scarce.

items.title: Dive in two turns: what it is safe from while aloft or under
items.body: Your 13:12 #3 ("like pokemon"), built: once a fight, at its swing, a diver with an enemy unit in its row rises (a Flyer; a Sprinter leaps the same way) or goes under (a Tide unit without wings) instead of swinging. Until its next swing nothing can find or hit it (swings, shots, bolts, skills aimed at a unit; a Spotter neither) and it can't step in as a Guardian. Its next swing strikes the weakest enemy of its row past Taunt (a Guardian beside the target still steps in) for Attack + N, and it is Exposed that round (no Flying dodge, no Tide evade). Area damage that names no target (a field's hail, a Nova, the tide-spout) and its own Poison / Bleed ticks still reach it, as in the games you described (Earthquake hits Dig in some, not Fly). A diver that can't strike in the next round (frozen, stunned) comes down at that round's end without striking. Keep area damage reaching it, or make it safe from everything?
options: Safe from everything while aloft / under
items.outcome: Owner, 2026-10-25 17:53: "don't build this first." Kept as built (area damage still reaches a diver); no further work now.

items.title: Poison / Bleed on extra hits, and "– poison" shots
items.body: Your 13:12 #5 ("common sense, not too overpowered"), built: a unit's Poison N / Bleed N (with Rabid, Greater Poison, Hemorrhage, Venom Master) ride on every landed hit of its own attack damage: the swing, Frenzy's and Twin Strike's swings, Fork / Trident / Pitchfork prongs and Octolash lashes (these already did), and now Pounce and Ambush (which did not). Cleave's side damage is a spread of the swing (an area, as for Guardian): it carries none. A shot or action (Arrow, Fire Arrow, a Bolt, Missile, Deal damage, Volley, Snipe ...) carries none, unless the card says "– poison" / "– bleed" on it (card text "Arrow 2 – poison"; a box on the Arrow, Missile and Deal damage actions in the card editor, as "– bramble"); it then gives the unit's own N, at least 1. Prices (4-round rule): Pounce / Ambush on a Poison or Bleed card pay 0.33 / 0.3 x the status's price on top (no card has both today); "– poison" on a shot 0.9 x Poison's price at that N (Arrow 2 – poison on a plain unit: +2.7). OK?
items.outcome: Owner, 2026-10-25 17:53: "Cleave and related DOES spread the status. I think arrow is okay. price = your decision." Queued: OWN-E7.

items.title: The state skills' prices and cards (Timbered, Bedrock, Forged, Last Stand)
items.body: Stone and Metal are real counts in a fight (pitching a Stone card, Quarry, the Petrified Tree's Stone, the Ore-Smelter Mole's Metal; Stone / Metal costs spend them), so the skills read them directly. Measured how often each state holds (docs/balance/en5-state-uptime-2026-10-24.json, 2000 CPU fights of random live decks): 3+ Lumber 0.9% of unit-rounds (the CPU spends Lumber as it comes), 2+ Stone 0.5% even with 4 Stone makers (one card makes Stone), 1+ Metal 83% with 4 Metal makers, 0.9% without, the bramble at a third or less 10%. Priced by your 4-round rule x the uptime a deck built for it would have: Timbered {+0/+2} 2 x 0.25 = 0.5, Bedrock {Armor 1} 1.5 x 0.2 = 0.3, Forged {+1/+0} 2 x 0.5 = 1.0, Last Stand {+1/+1} 3 x 0.2 = 0.6 (the robust test read plain Last Stand 0.62, Timbered 0.38). Their braces cost the same uptime x the braces. Cards: Lodge Engineer (Timbered), Quarry Mole (Bedrock), Badger Trench Digger (Last Stand); no Forged card (the only Metal maker, the Ore-Smelter Mole, already has two skills and would hold Forged nearly always).

items.title: Bleed and Poison: the measured curve flattens
items.body: Your BP-1: "price it according to your simulation. Note that bigger numbers make them stronger". tools/skill_test_robust.js --mono --multi, 3000 games a setup, with the units priced at a trial 1 a point so the decks stay off the floor (EN4's 'about 2' for Bleed 2 / Poison 2 came from decks priced at 5.2 that lost 97% of their games). Worth with companions at N 1 / 2 / 3 / 4: Bleed 3.5 / 6.2 / 6.6 / 6.3, Poison 2.9 / 5.7 / 5.9 / 5.4 (docs/balance/en5-bleed-poison-2026-10-24.md). Bigger numbers are stronger in all up to 3, but each point is worth less: the stack outlives the small units it lands on. Priced S(N) = 3.6 x N^0.6 (Bleed) and 3.0 x N^0.7 (Poison), a power curve through N 1-3: Bleed 3.6 / 5.5 / 7.0, Poison 3.0 / 4.9 / 6.5 (was 2.6 / 5.2 / 7.8 for both). So a Bleed 1 or Poison 1 card costs more than before and a Bleed 3+ card less. The actions (Bleed / Poison in triggers) and the family (Gash, Venomous, Rabid ...) are unchanged.

items.title: Equipment durability: defaults by rarity, and what it does to the pieces' prices
items.body: Built (package EQ2, from your EQ-1 'Durability with acid / Corrode wear'): every piece has durability, its card's own number or by rarity: Common and Uncommon 3, Rare to Super Rare 4, Epic and up 5. A hit on the wearer takes 1 (a swing, a shot, a bolt, a raid smack, a floor's burn; a Poison or Bleed tick is not a hit), an acid hit 2, each Corrode applied 2. At 0 it breaks: it leaves play and its stats and skills come off the unit (Health never below 1). A dropped or stolen piece keeps its wear. The 50% / acid-death rule you disliked is not used. Price (4-round rule, bramblewood-budget.js equipLifeMult): a piece lasts about its durability in rounds, so it counts min(durability, 4) / 4 of its stats and grant: x0.75 for the Common and Uncommon pieces, x1 from Rare. All ten pieces were already well under N; durability frees 0.6-2 points on the five Common / Uncommon ones (docs/balance/eq2-equipment-2026-10-24.json). No card was changed.

items.title: Dive: the simplest form (once a fight, the weakest unit of the row, no landing move)
items.body: Built (package EQ2, N21-5; your note: a diving flier is 'exposed', no 50% miss advantage while diving). From docs/ramming-proposal-2026-10-21.md option C, cut to its simplest: Dive N (N 1 by default): once a fight, the unit's swing goes to the weakest enemy unit (least Health, the nearest on a tie) in the row it faces, past any Taunt, for N more damage. A Guardian beside that unit still steps in. It does not move: no landing in the target's column. A diving Flyer is exposed for the rest of that round: attacks at it get no Flying dodge. Only a Flyer, a Tide unit or a Sprinter can have it (diveEligible). Priced 0.75 a point by the 4-round rule (N once = 0.5 N, the pick of the weakest +0.5, the exposure -0.25). No card has it yet.

items.title: Parasite as built, and the Clinging Leech
items.body: Your 10-21 note (docs/titles-transforms-2026-10-21.md): 'Hooks onto enemy units? Not just leech-attacking from our side. So you place onto an enemy such that their column would be in reach.' The rest was undefined, so package EQ2 proposed and built: a Parasite card may be played onto an enemy unit in your reach (the centre, or a column with or beside one of your units) instead of into your slot (it may still be played as a plain unit). It rides its host: no slot, blocks nothing, can't be hit. It waits its own Wait, then feeds as each round's fight begins: its Attack as a flat hit on the host (no dodge, no Armor, no Guardian), healing itself as much. One Parasite a host, never on a Structure. When the host dies it drops onto your side in that column if the slot is free, else into your graveyard. Priced 1 (the sure hit and the safety against no lane blocked and no bramble damage). The CPU hooks it onto the enemy in reach worth the most. New card: Clinging Leech (Uncommon, 1 Lumber, Wait 1, 4/9 by the budget, placeholder art), awaiting a source.

items.title: The Ambush: what stays locked, and until when
items.body: Built from 'Those ambush skirmishes should lock the previous path I was going for. But then they also shouldn't be connected by a link but instead float there. The moment they are observed (ambushed), they are permanently accessible': the Ambush has no trail to or from it and floats where the scout shoved you; it is open the moment it is seen and stays on the map for good, won or not. The fight it interrupted (3-2) is drawn as a locked fight ('Blocked by the ambush') and, since everything after it waits on 3-2, so is the rest of that path. It opens when the Ambush is WON. Losing it, leaving it or walking away does not open the path. Alternatives: open the path after you have merely fought the Ambush (a loss counts), or after the Ambush is left once.

items.title: The Bleed doubler's name, and when it doubles
items.body: Your 22:23 #7: "Do we have the skills that do extra damage to bleeding units, or even 2x their bleed." Hunter (Bleeding) already does the extra damage; the new skill doubles. Built as HEMORRHAGE 🩸²: its swing that lands on a Bleeding unit doubles the Bleed the unit already has, THEN its own Bleed (if any) adds. Doubling after its own Bleed instead would make a lone Bleed 2 card double its own cut every hit (2, 6, 14 ...), which runs away. items.title: How Greater Poison ticks
items.body: Your 22:23 #7: "when units are hit with Greater Poison - all existing poison is converted to greater poison. Greater poison only hits for 1 poison by default. Usually they have both GP and Poison." Built: Greater Poison N (N 1 by default) on the attacker; its swing that gets through turns ALL the Poison the target had before the hit into Greater Poison and adds N; the swing's own Poison then lands as plain Poison, for its next hit to turn. The status: (A, built) each stack deals 2 a round, then the stack loses 1, as Poison does: Poison twice over. Poison 3 deals 3+2+1 = 6; turned, 6+4+2 = 12. (B) its whole stack every round, never wearing off: that is Toxin, which the game already has, so B would make Greater Poison 'Poison that turns into Toxin'. (C) its stack every round, wearing off 1 every 2 rounds. A reads plainest and keeps Toxin its own thing. Cure takes Poison first, then Greater Poison; Poison Tick (Venom Pulse) ticks both; Hunter (Poisoned) counts it. Status pip: a violet 💀 beside the green ☠.
options: (B) its stack every round, never wears off (as Toxin)
(C) its stack every round, -1 every 2 rounds

The first build (2 a stack, -1 a round) is gone.

items.title: Prices for Hemorrhage, Greater Poison and Shore Up

SHORE UP 2.2: a front unit survives 2-3 hits over 4 rounds with about 1.5 allies beside it, so 3-4.5 Shield, about half of it soaking: 1.5-2 Health; measured 2.68 alone, 2.26 with companions; set at 2.2. HEMORRHAGE 2: on a target already Bleeding about half its hits, each doubling adds about the stack (1-3), about +1 Bleed a hit (Bleed 2.6 a stack) = 1.3-2.6, and nothing without Bleed around. GREATER POISON 2.5 (N 1; scale half; 1 a stack, never wears off, owner 23:45): beside Poison 2, the target's ticks over 4 rounds go from 2+3+4 = 9 to 3+5+7 = 15, about 6 more damage = 3 stat points if it lives all 4 rounds, about 2 at a usual 2/3; alone 1+2+3 = 6. PULSE (owner 23:45: Venom Pulse renamed, Poison AND Bleed tick): the Pulse action 1.3 a tick (on a target Poisoned about half its hits, about 2.5 a tick, and Bleeding about a third, about 2: about 1.9 damage a pulse), so Pulse 1 = On Hit 2.1 x 1.3 = 2.7 (Venom Pulse was 2.1); no card carries it, so nothing re-fits. items.title: Use the optimizer's Elo gap as the difficulty dial for skirmish decks?
items.body: The optimizer measures how far each fight deck sits below the best deck its map's cards can make (Elo = 400 log10(p / (1 - p)) of the optimum's fair head-to-head score; +200 = the optimum wins 76%, +400 = 91%). items.title: Bleed now fades at the round's end, after it bleeds
items.body: Your 19:27 #5: "before they TAKE the bleed or poison damage, they -1. They should take the damage first." Bleed lost its stack at each round's START (since 10-18), before the unit acted, so a Bleed 3 dealt 2 then 1 (3 in all) instead of 3, 2, 1 (6). Built: a Bleeding unit loses 1 stack at the END of a round in which it started Bleeding or bled; a stack that lands after its last action that round waits for the next round's end, so it is bled in full first. A Waiting unit (which can't bleed on its own actions) still loses 1 a round from its second round. Festering still holds it. The grey drop plays at the round's end. Poison was already right in the engine (the tick is the whole stack, then -1); the board showed the badge drop at the same instant as the damage, so it now drops about half a second after the damage. Card-matrix results change wherever Bleed is in play (see the CHANGELOG).

items.title: Shore Up, the opposite of hunkering down: three ideas (not built)
items.body: Your 19:27 #4: "New Skill: Shore Up, opposite of Hunker Down? What could they do?" There is no Hunker Down skill; the nearest is Cower (hit last turn: it hides in its shell or backs off, no attack) and Shell. Three ways to turn that round: (A) SHORE UP N, the mason: each hit it survives, its bramble gets N Health back (On Attacked 1.9 x Rebuild 0.2 a point = about 0.4 per N); it fights on, and the beating it takes props up the bramble. (B) SHORE UP, brace the line: when it is hit (and survives) it doesn't hide; the allies beside it get Shield 1 for the next round (On Attacked 1.9 x Shield 0.35 x 2 allies = about 1.3); Cower saves itself, this saves its neighbours. (C) SHORE UP N, dig in when left alone: at the start of a round after one in which nothing hit it, it gains Shield N, up to 2N (On Round Start 3.5 x Shield 0.35 x about half the rounds = about 0.6 per N); Cower fires after a hit, this after a quiet round. Prices are estimates from canonical/skill-costs.json; each would be measured with tools/skill_test_robust.js once built.

items.title: The end of each map: a pack of 3 + 1 faction pack (built ON)
items.body: Your 19:36 note ("i think at the end of each map, give a pack of 3 + 1 faction pack, corresponding to that map series") is built behind MAP_END_PACKS (on): a main map's last fight, first clear, gives a 3-card pack of that map's series (Maps 0-6 the Hedgerow Pouch's pool, 7-13 the Tidemire Chest's, 14+ the Highcrest Case's; new cards first) and one faction pack of your side (2 faction cards out of the faction pool + 1 pack card). It comes on top of the map's free pack where it has one. items.title: Fighting in the middle: a CPU lane preference (built), or a rule
items.body: Your 13:16 #2 / #11. Measured (tests/en2-cpu-side-sim-2026-10-23.js, Maps 0-5 skirmishes, 840 games a level; docs/balance/en2-cpu-side-*.json): the basic and smart CPUs had no left lean (37.7% left, 38.1% right of their units); the smartest leaned left (40.8% / 33.3%) because its ties always went left. Against a player who builds on one edge, the basic CPU already puts 54% of its units on that side. Built (modest): when the CPU has no kill or trade to make, its random slot is weighted to the middle three slots and to slots facing or beside your units; the smartest CPU gets a small middle bonus and breaks ties toward your units, else a coin. Result: the smartest's lean is gone (mean slot -0.18 -> +0.01), contested placements +1.5 to +3 points, the CPU's win rate down about 2 points. A stronger push would have to be a rule both sides feel, e.g. +1 Attack for units in the middle three slots, or the bramble taking half from the outer lanes.
options: Add a middle-lane rule for both sides (+1 Attack in the middle three)
items.outcome: Owner, 2026-10-23 19:30: "I agree with your EN series" / "Okay to the gameplay ones." As built / as recommended (default: The CPU preference only (built)).

items.title: How should equipment be damaged or removed: durability worn by hits and acid (recommended), or another design?
items.body: Owner (10-23 11:11): "New: How to deal damage to equipment. (They do not have 'health stats'.) If the opponent has many equipment on the field, they act as perma buffs (albeit activating only 1 turn later). I don't think this rule is fun: 'When an equipped creature dies, the equipment has 50% chance to be destroyed. If defeated by acid damage, the equipment is 100% destroyed'" The rule today (bramblewood-engine.js, eqDrop, package EQ 10-19): the quoted 50% / acid rule is not in the engine or the texts. When the wearer dies, the piece stays in its slot and the next unit played there picks it up (Codex: "it stays when its unit dies"). It goes to the graveyard only if its card has equip.breaks, or if the slot already holds a loose piece. A reviving unit keeps its piece. A loose piece cannot be hit (swings pass it to the bramble). The only answer is Disarm (Glintsnatch Magpie), which steals a piece. So equipment is close to a permanent buff, as you say. Alternatives. (A) Durability: each piece has 2-4 durability pips. It loses 1 each time its wearer takes a hit (or, for weapons, each swing) and breaks at 0. A dropped piece keeps its pips. Pros: no randomness, hitting the wearer is the counterplay, readable. Cons: a new number on every equipment card and in the budget. (B) Corrosion: acid hits and Corrode strip durability (or destroy a loose piece outright), and fire burns wooden pieces. Pros: gives acid its own job and uses existing statuses. Cons: alone it answers equipment only for acid decks. (C) A Sunder family next to Disarm: Sunder N (On Hit: the target's piece loses N durability, or breaks if it has none), Shatter (On Play: break the nearest loose enemy piece), and Demolisher also hits loose pieces. Pros: a deck-building answer. Cons: if few cards carry it, pieces stay permanent buffs. (D) Pieces drop and rust: when the wearer dies, the piece lies loose for 2 rounds, then rusts away unless a unit of its side picks it up; the killer's Disarm or Scavenge can claim it. Pros: keeps the drop-and-pick-up idea, ends permanent buffs. Cons: a timer to show on the board. Recommended: A with B folded in. Durability 3 by default (set per card), -1 each time the wearer is hit, -2 for an acid hit or each Corrode applied; dropped pieces keep their durability. Add C's Sunder to a few cards later.
options: Pieces drop and rust after 2 rounds (D)
Break on the wearer's death (equip.breaks for all)
items.outcome: Owner, 2026-10-23 19:30: "I agree with your EN series" / "Okay to the gameplay ones." As built / as recommended (default: Durability with acid / Corrode wear (A+B)).

items.title: Hero levels now need Materia: how much
items.body: Each Hero level needs a third of its XP from Materia crafts (your H2 rule, built in SX). A Hero that only fights stalls at about two thirds of a level. Cost: Lv 20 needs 7 crafts (875 Dust), Lv 50 needs 44 (5,500), Lv 100 about 240 (30,000). Recommended: as built for now; add Materia XP from quests / raids if the pace feels slow.
options: A smaller Materia part (e.g. Battle 45%, Materia 20%, Either 35%)
items.outcome: Default taken (DC3, 2026-10-23): Equal thirds, as built: each Hero level needs a third of its XP from Materia crafts; more Materia XP sources (quests, raids) get added if the pace feels slow.

items.title: The battle rating counts an enemy leader at the enemy's level; it fights at its printed level
items.body: The BR counts a leader twice, at the fight's enemy level, but the CPU's reserve leader plays at the card's printed level (as SK's skirmish leaders already did). A boss unit of high rarity therefore raises the BR by up to 50% while the fight gets only about 6 points harder for the DF ant deck. Built (LEAD): BR within 5% on 110 of 112 fights. To get there, decks lost a copy or two, 57 fights got a lower enemyLevel and 23 a smaller or bigger enemy bramble, which brought the win rates back (400 games a fight, 95 of 112 within 3 points). Two named exceptions: 20-R (an all-Common deck, BR 20 -> 22) and 20-A-3 (36 against 38).
options: Count an enemy leader at the level it fights at (every Map 2+ skirmish's BR drops a little)
Make enemy leaders fight at the enemy's level (harder fights everywhere; needs a retune)
items.outcome: Claude's call (10-23, owner asked to settle the easy ones): As built, kept as built (the BR counts a leader at the enemy level, held within 5% by the retune).

items.body: The CPU saves Lumber only for cards in its hand, never for its reserve leader, so costly leaders (Marshal Tuskwell 4, the Magnate Duck 4, Gorge Wyrm 3) never came out in 60 test fights, while cheap ones came out in most. items.title: Deck slot prices
items.body: Built (UI4, your 01:03 note 5): a new player has 1 deck slot; more are bought in order in the Camp (under My Decks) or the Tavern's Upgrades tab. Slot 2: 150 Magic Dust + 150 Maple Leaves. Slot 3: 300 Dust + 250 Leaves. Slot 4 (Map 15 cleared): 600 Dust + 350 Leaves + 1 River Pearl + 1 Tempering Stone (Map 15's boss pays both on its first clear). Slot 5 (Map 21 cleared): 900 Dust + 450 Leaves + 1 Ember Core (from the Map 20 raid / world bosses). Slot 6 (Map 27): 1200 + 600 + 2 Ember Cores. Slot 7 (Map 33): 1500 + 750 + 1 Strange Materia + 1 Ember Core. Maps 27 and 33 are still Reserved, so slots 6-7 wait for them. Map 21's own fights pay only Iron Shards, so slot 5 asks for the Ember Core the road pays just before it. Existing saves keep every deck they have (their slots start at their deck count); a deck pulled from the cloud raises the slots the same way.

No cap past slot 7 (keep adding at the slot 7 price)

items.title: Swarm in the hand's blue numbers: 4 or 5 for an Ant Scout with 3 ants out
items.body: Built (UI4, your 01:57 note 11): a hand card shows in blue the Attack / Health it would have if played now, worked out by the engine's own rules (engine previewPlayStats). The engine's Swarm counts the OTHER allies that share a type, so an Ant Scout (1 Attack) with 3 ants out shows 1 + 3 = 4; your example said 1 + (3+1) x 1 = 5, which would count the scout itself. Also: a card whose skill depends on where it stands (Formation, Sociable, Lone Wolf) is previewed in the slot a plain play takes (the centre first, then the right end).

Count the card itself too (a rule change for every Swarm card in fights)

items.outcome: Owner (10-23 11:11): "Okay good catch. you're right." As built: Swarm counts the other allies only, so the Ant Scout with 3 ants out shows 4; no rule change.

items.title: Difficulty doesn't climb: from Map 16 the road gets easier, not harder
items.body: Measured on all 179 fights of Maps 0-24 (docs/balance/df-2026-10-23.json): the road gets easier from Map 16, not harder. The ant deck wins 64-74% of skirmishes on Maps 0-15 but 88-96% on Maps 16-24; a collected deck 81%. Causes: your level climbs 1 -> 8 between Maps 10 and 16 while the enemy's climbs 2 -> 3.2; the level curve is stepped; and every map's targets restart at 90% -> 40%. A trial 'pace' curve (the enemy 0.5-2.5 levels under your Forge cap) lowers Maps 16-24 skirmishes to 88% (ant) / 73% (collected). Recommended: the pace curve, plus DF-3's boons, plus targets that drift down across maps (first skirmish 90% on Map 1 to about 80% on Map 24), retuned against the ant and collected decks.
options: The pace enemy curve, plus DF-3's selfish effects, plus road targets that drift down across maps (each map's first skirmish 90% on Map 1 to about 80% on Map 24), retuned against the ant and collected decks
No level change: get the climb from DF-3 and from retuning each fight against the ant and collected decks
items.default: The pace enemy curve, plus DF-3's selfish effects, plus road targets that drift down across maps (each map's first skirmish 90% on Map 1 to about 80% on Map 24), retuned against the ant and collected decks
items.outcome: Owner (10-23 17:34): "Ill evaluate this when my new account progresses to that point. Map MUST absolutely contribute at 0.2* per Map. In the backend, I think you define Map as the reward source. But for Pack rewards - what source do you select? If its a Pack reward, select the first Map it appears (along the main line, not submaps). 20*0.2=4, a reasonable bonus. This may be enough to balance stronger maps and also make them appealing." Two rules for the stat budget: (1) the Map term is 0.2 per map (bramblewood-budget.js has perMap 0.1 since BF6 halved the coefficients, so it goes back to 0.2: a Map 20 card gets +4 N); (2) a pack card's map is the first main-line map it appears on, never a submap (today cardObtainMap uses the map where its pack goes on sale). New work: a balance package sets perMap 0.2, changes the pack rule in cardObtainMap, regenerates canonical/card-obtain-maps.json and re-fits the cards (docs/action-items.md, 10-23 17:34). Which climb fix goes in (the pace curve or another option) waits for his own play-through: DF-1b.
items.buildNote: Built by BAL2 (2026-10-24): perMap 0.2 (bramblewood-budget.js, canonical/skill-costs.json). "Appears on" is read as OBTAINABLE on that main-line map, as a reward or out of a pack there: a basic-pack card counts from the earlier of its pool map (the base track and the card drop; a side map at the main map that unlocks it) and the first main map that pays its pack (the end-of-map packs: Pack 1 Map 0, Pack 2 Map 7, Pack 3 Map 14), never before its rarity reveals on the main road (rarityIntroMap now reads ROAD_MAIN_FROM: Epic 22, Heroic 25); a map reward counts at the main map that unlocks its map. So Pack 1 cards count as Map 0 (they come out of Map 0's end pack), Pack 2 as Map 7, Pack 3 as Map 14: 339 cards' map moved down, 17 up, and with the doubled coefficient most map cards gained N. canonical/card-obtain-maps.json regenerated. Re-fit (tools/bal2_refit_2026_10_24.js): 254 cards on their old line rose to the new one, 36 over the new budget went down, 10 cuts over 25% held at their stats (alley-cat, honey-badger-fury, chipmunk-hoarder, chipmunk-cavalry, pyroclast-wyrm, plague-gnat-cloud, sunfeather-scout, lone-grey-wolf, rock-pool-starfish, muskrat-lodgekeeper) and 15 with no legal line kept; both lists merged into docs/balance/human-pass-1-flagged-2026-10-21.json. docs/balance/bal2-refit-2026-10-24.json lists every move.

items.title: Levels gate by map, not by resources; Base decks never need replacing
items.body: Model in docs/balance/df-2026-10-23.json: every deck reaches the Forge cap on the map that opens it (Lv 3 at Map 11, Lv 8 at Map 16), light or binge player alike, so levels gate by map, not by resources. What holds decks back is duplicates outside Base (about 56 repeat fights for one more copy of a common), so the strongest deck is a cheap Base synergy deck that never needs replacing. Recommended: Base cards stop at Lv 4 and pay full Forge cost; a fight's own first-clear card drops 10% a repeat, so 4-copy decks form by about Maps 10-15.
options: Base cards stop at Lv 4 and pay full Forge cost (x1); a fight's own first-clear card drops 10% a repeat (was 3% x its rarity share), so 4-copy decks form by about Map 10-15
Base cards stop at Lv 4 only
Slow the Forge instead: the Ember Forge (Map 16) caps at Lv 6, Lv 8 from Map 21
items.default: Base cards stop at Lv 4 and pay full Forge cost (x1); a fight's own first-clear card drops 10% a repeat (was 3% x its rarity share), so 4-copy decks form by about Map 10-15
items.outcome: Owner (10-23 17:34): "DF-2 OKAY. But of course, don't look down on the grind they have to do to level up their cards to that tier's gate." The recommended option: Base cards stop at Lv 4 and pay the full Forge cost (x1), and a fight's own first-clear card drops 10% a repeat (was 3% x its rarity share), so 4-copy decks form by about Maps 10-15. His note: the model and the tuning must count the grind it takes to level cards up to each tier's gate, not treat reaching it as free. New work: a balance package (docs/action-items.md, 10-23 17:34).
items.buildNote: Built by BAL2 (2026-10-24): Base cards (source Base, starters, tutorial and basic cards) stop at Lv 4 (BASE_CARD_LEVEL_CAP: the Forge, the boss growth, no limit break or Prestige; the Forge says so) and pay x1 (canonical/upgrade-costs.json modifiers.base; quest and map cards keep x0.5); the reference player's Base cards stop at Lv 4 too. A skirmish's own first-clear card drops 10% of its repeat wins, any rarity (SKIRMISH_OWN_REPEAT_DROP), else the pack card at the plain 1%. Elites keep their tier drop (the own-card roll is a skirmish's, as GD built it). The grind to each gate: docs/progression-plan.md (tools/bal2_grind_2026_10_24.js).

The Environment card shows the count ('11/16 Cave', red outline, a 'theirs' mark). 15 boons are proposed (e.g. Map 8 Blind Fury: Cave units deal 2x in Darkness; Map 17 Frostborn; Map 24 Royal Treasury); Maps 6, 11, 14, 15 and 21 get none. Only on elites, mini-bosses and bosses
On skirmishes too, but only from Map 10

A 3/7 Armor 1 Beetle Grunt hit 4, 4, 2 shows 3, 3, 1 and dies at exactly 0; in 13 auto-played 0-4 fights the shown Health matched the engine after every hit and round and every death played at 0 (screens in docs/screens/PG; the final hit shows its number and Health 0 together). items.title: Guardian's front / behind is raid-board only
items.body: In front / behind needs rows that fight, so it applies on the raid board (3 rows, every row acts). Elsewhere a reserve row is only waiting to step up (not on the battlefield), so a Guardian waiting there doesn't guard the unit in front of it, and nothing guards a waiting unit. Normal fights have one row, so they only have left / right (the card matrix shows 0 changed fights); in 600 random raid-board fights with Guardians, 508 ended differently.
items.outcome: Owner 19:27: "GD-1: From now on, things that deal with L/R can just say 'adjacent' e.g. Formation cares about adjacent units. Adjacent is defined as behind, in front, left, right. Only relevant in raids or multi-player dungeons. (I see that Guardian's short desc is already correct)" Built (package GD2): one engine helper, adjacentOf (bramblewood-engine.js): left and right in a unit's own row, plus directly in front / behind only where every row fights (the raid board, RESERVE_ACTS); elsewhere just left / right, so ordinary fights play exactly as before. On it: Guardian, the new Spellshield, Formation (a waiting reserve no longer counts), Haste, Shieldwall, Amplifier, Immolation, Irradiated, Inspiring, Friction, Proliferate, Electricity, Chain Lightning, Dragon Lightning, Spitfire's splash and a trigger's Adjacent Ally target. Their texts and the Codex term say "adjacent" (12 packs). Column shapes keep their columns (call GD2-5). Owner (10-23 11:11): "Adjacent - Up/Down/Left/Right; Surrounding - include diagonals -> Okay!" Confirmed as built.

items.title: Which Guardian steps in: left, right, in front, behind
items.body: When two or more Guardians are next to the target, the first in this order takes the hit: left, right, the one in front, the one behind (the old rule was left before right). A Guardian never guards itself, but a Guardian next to another Guardian is guarded by it.
options: As built (left, right, in front, behind)
In front first (it stands between the enemy and the target)
items.default: As built (left, right, in front, behind)
items.outcome: Owner 19:27: "GD-2: Random," Built (package GD2): when two or more Guardians are adjacent to the target, one of them takes the hit at random (the fight's seeded RNG, so replays repeat; it only rolls with two or more, so a fight with one Guardian draws the same numbers as before).

items.title: Status-only skills still go to the unit they aim at
items.body: Guardian takes single-target hits: a swing, an arrow or another shot, and a skill that deals damage to one target. A skill that only puts a status on one enemy (Poison, Expose, Stun, Bleed or Add Wait aimed at one unit) is not redirected, as before. Area hits are never redirected.
options: A Guardian also takes single-target statuses
items.outcome: Owner 19:27: "GD-3: AOE can't get redirected. Status only skills hmm. I think if it's skills (including arrow), guardianship doesn't help. So no redirection for skills. We have ward for dodging skills right? There can be a similar skill - but for shielding allies from skills." Built (package GD2): Guardian redirects plain swings only: a unit's basic attack and the prongs of that swing (Fork, Trident, Pitchfork, Octolash: each prong is a full single-target swing). Cleave's side damage is a spread of the swing, so not redirected, as before (call GD2-2). Arrows (Arrow, Archer, Snipe), Bolts, shots, damage and status skills reach their target; areas never redirect. New skill Spellshield 🪬 (call GD2-1 for the name): a single-target enemy skill aimed at an adjacent ally hits the Spellshield unit instead. There is no Ward that dodges skills in the game: the closest are Helmet (deflects half the shots aimed at it) and Evasive.

items.title: 💥 is the crit mark; the hit burst keeps 💥
items.body: On numbers and log lines 💥 now means a crit only: Explode's fuse line and its "Boom!" float use 💣, Stampede's log line and its carry-over preview (+N) use 🐘. The quick burst that flashes on a card when it's hit by a physical attack is still a 💥, with no number on it (elemental hits show their own glyph). The raid smack's log line ("💥 X sweeps your front row"), "💥 Crash!" and "👑💥 King Slayer!" keep theirs (words, not a number).
options: Change the hit burst too (e.g. a white spark)
Change every other 💥 in the battle
items.outcome: Owner 19:27: "GD-4: King Slayer: 🗡️, Fencer: 🤺" Built (package GD2): King Slayer's float is "🗡️ King Slayer! +N" (was 👑💥); a Fencing unit's plain hit bursts as 🤺 instead of 💥 (Fencing had no float or log mark of its own; the hit burst was its 💥).

items.title: Skirmishes whose first clear is a pack or a token: 7%
items.body: Every first-clear reward card a skirmish pays today is skirmish-only (since RP, a map's reward cards are never pack cards), so the tripled drop covers those skirmishes. A skirmish whose first clear gives a pack or a Faction Reward / Growth token has no single card to drop, so it has the plain 7% pack-card drop on every win (it had none). If a skirmish is ever given a pack card as its reward, the same 21% rule picks it up.
items.outcome: Owner 19:27: "GD-5: No. There should be a mix of 'no first clear card', 'first clear skirmish-exclusive card', 'first clear pack card reward' and of course pack rewards.. Skirmish exclusive makes up 1-2 (max 3). The rest are a mix of the rest. If it turns out there is not much left, then okay." Built (package GD2): a skirmish's first clear can pay a pack card of its own map (SKIRMISH_FIRST_PACK_CARDS, written by tools/gd5_first_cards_2026_10_22.js; the card stays a pack card). The exclusive cards stay where they were (every map had 0-2). The other skirmishes alternate pack card / none: of 101 main-map skirmishes, 23 pay an exclusive card, 44 a pack card (each one from that fight's own deck), 1 a pack (0-2), 33 nothing. A pack-card skirmish drops like an exclusive one: 7% on its first clear, 21% on repeats with that card at its rarity share. Calls GD2-3, GD2-4. docs/balance/gd5-first-cards-2026-10-22.json.

items.title: The drop line shows the reward card's chance per win
items.body: A cleared skirmish's drop line reads, for a Common reward card: (card) 13% · 🃏 8.4%, its chance a win (21% x 60% = 12.6%, rounded as the line rounds above 10%) and the pack card's share. Before the first clear it reads 🃏 7% (the card itself is in the First Clear box).
options: Show 🃏 21% and the card's share of it (60%)
items.outcome: Owner 19:27: "GD-6: Sounds correct I think? For skirmish first-clear reward card drops - they don't roll twice. They just roll for the skirmish-exclusive, then if they get it, they roll within it to see if they get another card instead." Checked (package GD2): rollCardDrop already does exactly this: one roll at 21% on a repeat win, then within it the reward card's rarity share (Common 60% ...), else a pack card; no second roll (a Common reward: 12.6% the card, 8.4% a pack card; 20,000 seeded rolls in tests/gd2-2026-10-22.js). Nothing changed. The panel line shows the per-win chance, as built.

items.title: An elemental crit shows only its big glyph, no 👊
items.body: Read from "can you just make the damage type emoji bigger if it's non physical": an ice crit on a Fragile unit now reads (big ❄️)14🦴 (DN had 👊❄️14🦴). A physical crit keeps 👊7. One switch brings the fist back on elemental crits (DMG_CRIT_FIST_ON_ELEMENT).

items.body: Following the rule (type glyph, none for physical), numbers that used to show their source now show their type: an Arrow Slits arrow, a trap, Pierce, Stampede, Friction, a Penance / Blood Tithe payment and the tentacle's stamp are plain numbers (was 🏹 🪤 🗡 💥 ⚙️ ⛧ 🦑); a comet or scorched ground is 🔥 (was ☄️ 🌋); Decay is 🍂 (was 🦠). Ticks with no element keep their own glyph: Curse 🜏, Chilli 🌶️, Strangle 🪢. The skill's own effect (the tentacle, the arrow, the spark) still plays.
options: Keep a source glyph on physical-only sources (🏹 🦑 🪤)
items.outcome: Owner (10-23 00:10): "Yes." As built: damage numbers lead with the damage type.

items.body: A crit's log line now reads "hit X for 👊14🦴 ❄️ cold damage" instead of "... for 14 ❄️ cold damage 💥 Crit!". An Ambush hit (no 👊 on its floating number either) keeps the words.
items.outcome: Owner 18:20: "DN2-3: 💥 is a better symbol for Crit to me." Built (package GD): 💥 replaces 👊 as the crit mark on floating numbers, bramble hits, the battle log ("hit X for 💥14🦴 ❄️ cold damage"), the Codex's "reading damage numbers" line and DN2's constants (DN_CRIT_MARK). Other 💥 that sat on a number or a log line moved off it: Explode's fuse line and its "Boom!" float are 💣, Stampede's log line and its carry-over preview (+N) are 🐘.

items.title: "Higher hue" is +12 degrees for every element
items.body: Built as asked (lighter by 10%, hue +12 degrees). Fire turns a brighter yellow-orange and magic a pinker violet, but ice turns slightly bluer (its hue is already past cyan), not the lighter cyan I described at 15:39. Poison greens turn a little bluer too.

items.outcome: Owner (10-23 00:10): "Okay. Maybe poison turns a little less bluer than it would do, and abit brighter instead." Keep +12 degrees for every element, but poison's shift is eased so it goes less blue and a little brighter. To build in package SX. Built (SX): DMG_CRIT_BY_CLASS = {poison: {hue: 5, lighten: 0.16}} next to DN2's knobs; poison (and acid and decay, which share its colours) turns +5 degrees and 16% lighter (its crit number is a light yellow-green, hsl 100 65% 70%, not teal); every other element keeps +12 degrees and 10%.

items.title: Hit numbers drop the minus sign; the other damage numbers keep theirs
items.body: Package DN follows the note's format exactly ("🔥20⛨"), so a unit hit now reads 🔥3⛨, 👊7, 👊❄️14🦴, 5 (was 🔥 -3, -7, 👊❄️ -14). The other damage numbers are separate code and keep their old look with a minus: Bleed and Poison ticks, field damage (comets, lava, hail, the tentacle's 🦑 −2), bramble hits on the HP bar, Reflect and Thorns. Colours are unchanged everywhere.

Put the minus back on hits
items.outcome: Owner 15:39: "DN-1 Yes. DN-3 OKAY. DN-4 Yes. DN-2 Im now thinking, can you just make the damage type emoji bigger if it's non physical. e.g. wand for magic becomes big if its crit! or even colour burn it abit? What would the color of the text be btw? a 10% lighter and higher hue version of the original color?" Built (package DN2): every damage number reads <type glyph><number><mark> with no minus: Poison / Bleed / Decay / Toxin / Strangle / Curse / Chilli ticks, field damage (scorched ground, eruption, comets, lava, hail, ley lines, the depths, arrow slits, landslide), bramble hits on the HP bar (Bulwark is the ⛨), Pierce and Stampede, Reflect / Thorns, Friction, Recoil, Ichor, traps, the meteor's crater, Fire on hit, the firepot, splash, and the raid's Tentacle Smack / Tail Sweep stamps. The engine adds the marks (mods) to those events; no number changed (card matrix: 0 diffs). Heals keep their look.

items.title: The marks after a hit number, and which one wins
items.body: One mark per hit, the strongest: 🚫 immune (the hit did 0 because of Immune, Invincible or a Cower shell), then ⛨ blocked to 0 by Armor, then 🦴 Fragile, then 💢 Weakness (also Shocked, which takes ×1.5), then ⛨ any reduction (Armor, Resist, Sturdy, Shell / temporary Health, stone, Rage's half, Scare, Ghost / Atheist halving). The engine now tags each hit with why its number moved (`mods` on the hit event, display only). ⛨ is a text symbol (no emoji exists), drawn in steel with a dark edge.
options: Separate marks for Armor and Resist
Show two marks when an up and a down both apply
items.outcome: Owner 15:39: "DN-1 Yes. DN-3 OKAY. DN-4 Yes. DN-2 Im now thinking, can you just make the damage type emoji bigger if it's non physical. e.g. wand for magic becomes big if its crit! or even colour burn it abit? What would the color of the text be btw? a 10% lighter and higher hue version of the original color?" Built (package DN2): the mark rule stays as built. A crit that isn't physical draws its type glyph 1.4x on a soft burn in the element's colour (no 👊), and its number takes the type's colours 10% lighter and 12 degrees up the hue wheel (DMG_CRIT_LIGHTEN 0.10, DMG_CRIT_HUE 12, DMG_CRIT_GLYPH_SCALE 1.4 in arena_app.js). Marks keep their size; a physical crit keeps 👊; normal hits keep their colours.

items.body: The note suggested ❇ for elemental crits unless the game already had a crit mark. It does: 👊 (since 2026-10-08). So a physical crit reads 👊7 and an ice crit on a Fragile unit reads 👊❄️14🦴.

Built (package DN2): battle-log damage lines carry the same marks after the number (🦴 💢 ⛨ 🚫) and 👊 before a crit's number, and the element glyph where the line names the type ("took 3 ☠️ poison damage", "2 🧪 acid", "1 💭 psychic damage"). Wording otherwise unchanged; the marks sit inside the translated templates' values, so the 12 packs still match.

items.title: Which field effects count as "similar" to Crushing Depths (now 1 damage)
items.body: Set to 1 damage a round by default, and every map number brought down to 1: Crushing Depths (5; the raid's 2), Hail (3; maps 22-4, 22-7, 22-8 had 2), Glass-storm (random 1–3), Lava Spout (3; 22-5, 22-8 had 2), Leylines III (3 to units and brambles), Thunderstorm (2; 10-7, 10-9), Arrow Slits (2; 23-7 had 3, 24-5 and 24-8 had 2). Left alone: Landslide (1 in 4 rounds, 5 to three columns: a chance event, not every round), the volcano's hazards and Scorched Ground (boss mechanics), Tide-spout (already 1), Ash Rain (1 to brambles only).
items.outcome: Owner 14:12: "FX-1: Landslide 1/4 chance to deal 3. Volcano hazards - idk how much I wrote, but 5 may be the max dmg. The normal average damage over a turn cannot exceed 1 in this case." Built (package FX2): Landslide 1 in 4 for 3 (was 5; 0.75 a round on a unit in its columns). The volcano: Lava Tide 1 (was 3), Eruption 1 (was 2), comets 1 to every unit (was a random 2–5), Scorched Ground's editor preset 1 (was 2). Each hazard's number times its chance stays at or under 1 at every volcano level, and a map's own number is capped at 5. Measured on the only level the maps use (low, 22-6 and 22-8): 0.41 a unit a round from all three together (about 1.35 before). Call FX2-1 asks about the higher levels combined.

items.title: How a 1-damage Crushing Depths halves for Swimmers
items.body: Chosen: a halving keeps at least 1, so at 1 damage a Tide unit or Swimmer takes 1 like everyone. Only when both halvings stack (a Swimmer or Tide unit that also resists water) does it round down: 0 at 1 damage. Hail and Lava Spout keep the game's usual Resist rule (half, at least 1), so Resist does nothing against a 1.
options: Keep (at least 1; Swimmer + Water Resist takes 0)
items.default: Keep (at least 1; Swimmer + Water Resist takes 0)
items.outcome: Owner 14:12: "FX-2: we shall do normal rounding. if x < 0.5, 0; else 1. Is this fair? Only round once, when it comes into fruition on the battlefield. Internal calculations should never round. Even when passing numbers between functions. Idk how you code it internally - the first ApplyDamage(X) before damage calculation and etc. then the final real ApplyDamage(Y) which results in a literal ReduceHealth(Y) 1-1 + firing related triggers." Built (package FX2): damage is worked out exactly (Resist, Weakness, Fragile, Sturdy, Ghost / Supreme / Shade / Atheist halves, Shock x1.5, Rage's half, stone, Armor, a row's half share, Bloodlust, half lines, Stagger, the Psychic Dampener, a Swimmer's half in the Crushing Depths) and rounded once, half up, in applyDamage, the one place a unit's Health goes down for a hit (damageHQ for a bramble). So a Swimmer at 1 takes 0.5 -> 1, a water-resistant Swimmer 0.25 -> 0, as this call's default had it; a 3 into Resist now lands 2 (was 1), a 5 lands 3 (was 2). The "at least 1" after a factor or a half is gone (it was a patch for rounding down).

items.title: The Tail Sweep: purple tentacle now, but still always your front row for 3
items.body: The green "worm" on PC was the Tail part's Tail Sweep, which always hits your front row (its rule, at every width). It is now drawn as the purple tentacle along the front row. Its damage (3 every 2 turns) is its own data and was not changed. The Tentacle Smack (arms and Core) is 1–2 now in the raid fight; the classic trench mode keeps its 6.
options: Keep the Tail Sweep as is
Tail Sweep picks a random row like the Smack
items.default: Keep the Tail Sweep as is
items.outcome: Owner 14:12: "FX-3: Raids hit too hard. Tail sweep for 2 instead? If its supposed to be the stronger attack among the first 3 fights before the core, okay. Otherwise, 1-2. The weaker attacks should just be 1 (AOE). Non AOE attacks can go up to 3, but in this case, there isn't." Built (package FX2): the Tail Sweep is the strongest AOE attack of the first three fights (your whole front row, every 2 turns), so it deals 2 (was 3). The Tentacles' Tentacle Smack (a column or a row, every 3 turns) is a weaker AOE attack: 1 (FX had 1–2). There are no single-target boss attacks. The Core's smack keeps FX's 1–2 (call FX2-2). The classic trench now uses the same numbers (no trenchDmg 6); its balance test holds with the Core's trench bramble at 300 (was 200). The Tail Sweep stays on your front row.

items.title: The volcano's hazards together, at its higher levels
items.body: Each hazard alone stays at or under 1 a unit a round (Lava Tide, Eruption, comets and Scorched Ground are 1 each). Together, measured with 3 units a side over rounds 2–20: very low 0.10, low 0.41 (the only level the maps use), medium 0.64, rising ("even") 1.19, high 1.34, because after an eruption comets hit every unit for 3 rounds and at the higher levels eruptions come almost every round. The most one unit took in one round was 3 (a comet, an eruption and lava together).
options: Comets 1 in 2 rounds at the higher levels
Cap the volcano at 1 a unit a round in total
items.outcome: Owner (10-23 00:10): "After eruptions, it restarts to very low again." Not one of the three options: the volcano's level falls back to very low after each eruption and climbs again, instead of rising to the higher levels and staying there. To build in package EN. Built (EN): after each Eruption the volcano is Very Low the next round and climbs one level a round back to its own (Very Low, Low, Medium, Even, High); an Even volcano rises again from there. The forecast carries the level (volcanoLevel). How fast it climbs is call EN-7.

items.title: The Core's Tentacle Smack keeps 1–2
items.body: Your rule covers the first three fights (the Tentacles and the Tail): the Tail Sweep 2, the Tentacles' smack 1. The Core is the fourth fight, so its smack keeps FX's 1–2 (a seeded 50/50, shown on the tentacle). In the classic trench (admins only) a smack doesn't roll, so the Core's is 2 there.
items.outcome: Owner 18:20: "FX2-2: OKAY". Kept as built: the Core's Tentacle Smack stays 1–2.

items.title: A half of 1 is 1: Resist, Ghost, Atheist and the Psychic Dampener no longer stop a 1
items.body: Under one rounding half up, a single halving of 1 is 0.5 and lands as 1, so Resist, a Ghost's, Supreme's or Shade's half, Atheist and the Psychic Dampener do nothing against a 1-point hit or tick (a Ghost took 0 from a 1-point poison tick before; a dampened Psychic 1 did nothing; now both are 1). Two halvings (0.25) still come to 0. Across the card matrix's 30,680 fights, 488 changed, 48 of them changed winner, all from this kind of rounding.
options: Round halves down only for a 1 (a resisted 1 is 0)
Bring back "at least 1" with rounding down
items.outcome: Owner 18:20: "FX2-3: OKAY as is". Kept as built: one rounding half up, so a halved 1 lands as 1.

Nothing was changed here.

items.title: Skirmishes with a first-clear reward: no card drop, repeats included
items.body: N22-5 gave the pack-card drop to "skirmishes with no pack or card reward", and RW2 keeps that: a skirmish whose first clear pays a card, a reward token or a free pack never drops a card, not even on a repeat win. Before RW2 those skirmishes still had the old 10% enemy-card drop (RW-3 moved every fight to the one pack drop, so they now have none). Elites and bosses drop on every win.
options: They drop on repeat wins only (7%)
items.outcome: Owner 18:20: "RW2-1: Yes. There are two kinds of first-clear drop card reward skirmishes: skirmish-exclusive, or from that map range's pack. ALL skirmishes have a low chance to get a card from the pack. For skirmishes, the chance of getting a card is tripled. But you mostly (50+%) get THAT card. (If it's higher in rarity, then the chance actually decreases - your call. Maybe 60/50/40/25/20/10/5/4/3/2/1..." Built (package GD): every skirmish win, first clear and repeats, rolls the pack-card drop at 7% (a skirmish paying a card, a token or a pack no longer drops nothing). items.title: When an evolute dies, do the cards under it fire their On Death?
items.body: Built: no. The whole stack goes to the graveyard (or the Removal Zone, wherever the evolute goes) and only the top card's own death effects happen (its On Death, Bounty, Relic ...). The cards under it fire nothing, matching "a unit leaving play this way triggers no On Death, Bounty or grave effects".
options: No: only the top card's death effects
Yes: each card in the stack fires its own On Death (top first)
items.default: No: only the top card's death effects
items.outcome: Owner (10-23 00:10): "No." Only the top card's death effects fire (the default). Built (EN): kept as built (only the top card's death effects fire).

items.title: Evolute bases: shared type at every stage, creatures only
items.body: Built: Alpha and Omega also need a shared type with their base (the rule named it for Evolute only). A plain Evolute cannot go over a unit that is already an evolute (no sideways or downward evolving). Structures, cages and a Gladiator leader are never bases, and only front-row units are (a raid's middle and back rows are not). The editor offers Evolute / Alpha / Omega on Evomax cards only.

Allow an Evolute over an evolute
items.outcome: Owner (10-23 00:10): "Yes. But just shared with what it is. Once evolved over, do not reference the card below. OKAY to the rest" Keep all of these (the default), with the type rule narrowed: the type is shared only with the card it sits on at that moment; once evolved over, the card below is no longer referenced. To build in package EN. Built (EN): kept; checked that a stage reads only the type of the card it goes over at that moment (its own derived card) and nothing reads the cards under it (they are only zone entries); the rule is now written in the engine's EV block.

items.title: An evolute waits its own Wait again

Not quite the default: the evolute waits its own Wait and, if it has Wait, also takes on the base's remaining Wait. To build in package EN. Built (EN): an evolute waits its own Wait plus the base's remaining Wait (a Ready base adds nothing); the CPU counts a waiting base's Wait against it.

items.title: The 3-part Hero XP bar (feedback item 17)
items.body: How the three XP bars should split (battle XP, Materia XP, ...?) — needs your picture of it.
items.outcome: Owner (10-23 00:10): "Battle XP, Materia XP, Battle XP OR Materia XP. But if you use Battle XP for the 3rd section, there is a 25% inefficiency." The Hero XP bar has three sections: Battle XP, Materia XP, and a third that takes either; filling the third with Battle XP is 25% less efficient. To build in package SX. Built (SX): each level's need (heroXpToNext) is split in thirds: Battle, Materia, Either. Battle XP fills only the first, Materia XP only the second; the third takes Materia 1:1 and Battle at 75% (HERO_XP_EITHER_BATTLE). A level is gained when all three are full; XP past a full part waits for the next level. The save keeps two pools (xpB, xpM since a base level, lvBase); h.xp stays the plain total. Old saves keep their level and their XP into it becomes Battle XP. The Hero Hall shows the three parts (Either split: Materia violet, Battle striped ember), the rule as the bar's tooltip and as a line under it, each part's numbers on hover. Calls SX-2, SX-3.

items.title: Siding with Otters or Hummingbirds: approve the proposal as written, or answer its questions (a)-(f) first?
items.body: (Rewritten 10-23 at the owner's request, all inside this item; the older siding-proposal-2026-10-08.md is source material, to move into the hub later.) What it is: the player is a traveller both peoples want on their side: the Otters (Rivergate Legion) and the Hummingbirds (Sunfeather Tribes). A hidden Standing number from -100 (Otters) to +100 (Hummingbirds) moves with the player's choices, and the band it sits in decides which rewards, titles, shops and story branches open. Where it lives today: the side picked in the tutorial is stored as `bramblewood_arena_faction` (saveFactionChoice / loadFactionChoice, arena_app.js) and today only sets the starter deck, the voice in warnings and the faction pack; cards carry `faction` (14 Hummingbird cards, 27 base) and `source.side` ('tribes', 'shared'); the faction reward track (noteFactionReceived) counts faction-pack pulls. Dialogue choices already exist (playDialogue with onDone replies, for example the Old Well in visitOldWell). Nothing reads a Standing yet. What siding changes for the player: (1) Reward cards: some skirmishes offer two reward cards, one per side; the player gets the one matching their band, Neutral gets a third (road-folk, dog or cat card). (2) Side shops: a Legion Quartermaster and a Tribe Trader on later maps, different stock. (3) Titles and character looks (Legion Outrider, Friend of the Tribes, Wanderer of Both Banks). (4) Materia leaning: Otter crafting nudges Shield/Formation, Hummingbird crafting Flight/Bond. (5) Story: dialogue warms or cools by band; from Map 6 a key skirmish plays differently by band; a Neutral track keeps the peace through a series of tests, hardest, with unique rewards. (6) It never locks a people's cards away: off-side cards stay in packs and the Market, only the story rewards differ; and nobody is punished for the tutorial pick. What moves Standing: dialogue choices +/-2 to 8 (no number shown on the button), first clears of one people's skirmishes +/-1 (fighting Otters drifts you to the Hummingbirds and the reverse), side quests +/-5 to 15 (a few per map, often exclusive), neutral acts (helping dogs, cats, road-folk, the Traveller) pull toward 0. Drift is slow: 2-3 maps of consistent choices to a friend band, most of the campaign to be Sworn. Five bands: Sworn Otter (<= -60), Otter friend (-59 to -20), Neutral (-19 to 19), Sunfeather friend (20 to 59), Sworn Sunfeather (>= 60); a two-coloured banner on Profile and the Conquest map shows the band. Build in four steps: (1) the Standing store (saved with the account), the banner and hidden weights on dialogue choices, Old Well first; (2) two-sided reward cards on 3-4 skirmishes of Maps 1-3, picked in the skirmish editor; (3) two side quests per map for Maps 1-3; (4) side shops from Map 4, titles, the Map 6 fork. Open questions for you: (a) start at +/-10 from the tutorial pick, or everyone at 0? (b) is the meter shown as a number or only as the band name? (c) is Neutral a full third path with its own ending, or only a resting place? (d) should the two-sided rewards and the side quests wait until the factions are symmetric (RP4), so neither side is the stronger pick? (e) how does siding interact with the Hummingbird gate (the faction pack) and the 0-2 faction pack? (f) can the player reset Standing, or does drift back by effort only? Options stay: Approve as written, Change parts, Not yet. Waiting for your pass over (a)-(f).

items.title: Which AI services should we set up, free tiers first, and will you create the accounts? (your browser; nothing bought)
items.body: Owner (10-23 17:38): "A1 description - list all the AIs that could help us, esp through omnirouting to gain utility without spending tokens." Researched 2026-10-23 (free limits change often; each is re-checked on its own page before use). The idea: send cheap or bulk work (translations, drafts, sim summaries, second-opinion reviews) to free tiers through one router, and keep Claude for design, engine and final review. Every account below is yours to create; Claude never creates accounts, enters passwords or buys anything, and no key goes into the repo or a chat (keys live as local environment variables). ROUTERS (one key, many models). (1) OpenRouter: 20+ ":free" models from several providers behind one OpenAI-style API; 20 requests/min and 50/day free, 1,000/day after a one-time $10 top-up (your call). Account: openrouter.ai. (2) LiteLLM (open source, runs on your machine): one local endpoint that routes to the free tiers below and falls back when one is rate-limited; no account. (3) Vercel AI Gateway: multi-provider with your own keys (BYOK), on the Vercel account you already have. FREE TEXT / CODE MODELS (behind a router). Google AI Studio (Gemini Flash / Flash-Lite and 2.5 Pro free; free-tier prompts may be used by Google to improve its products, fine for this public repo, not for secrets); Groq (about 30/min, 1,000/day; Llama 3.3 70B); Cerebras (about 1M tokens/day); Mistral (about 1B tokens/month, Codestral for code); GitHub Models (150-1,000/day, on your GitHub login); Cloudflare Workers AI; NVIDIA NIM. Use for us: first-draft translations of the 12 language packs, text and lore drafts, summarising sim logs, a second reviewer on diffs. Local and free with no account: Ollama with open models (Qwen, Llama, Gemma) on your own machine. TRANSLATION. DeepL API Free: 500,000 characters a month at no cost (account at deepl.com; it may ask for a card to verify, nothing is charged on Free). Good for checking the language packs against the English. CODE REVIEW. CodeRabbit: free reviews on public repositories with the paid-tier features for open source (sign in with GitHub); CodeQL already scans every push (S4). ART (beside PixelLab and NightCafe, already in use). ChatGPT image generation free daily cap (commercial use allowed by OpenAI's terms); Gemini "Nano Banana" free in the app (visible and invisible SynthID watermark, so drafts only); Ideogram about 10 slow credits/day (free images are public); Leonardo 150 tokens/day (free-tier images not for commercial use); Microsoft Copilot 15 fast boosts, then slower. Best use: concept drafts and splash/marketing comps, then PixelLab or the pixel pass for anything that ships. SOUND, MUSIC, VOICE. Stable Audio Open 1.0 (open weights, runs locally, up to 47 s, better at sound effects than music; Stability Community License, check stability.ai/license for commercial use); ElevenLabs free 10,000 credits a month (about 50 sound effects or 10 minutes of voice) but no commercial licence on free (Starter $6/month has it: your call); Suno free 50 credits/day (about 10 songs) but non-commercial and few downloads, so reference tracks only. For the shipped music (D17) CC0 packs remain the safe route. VIDEO (trailer, A3). Kling via fal stays the plan; it needs a paid key and a cap (below). PAID KEYS (only if you choose): OpenAI (platform.openai.com, set a monthly budget and alerts at 50% / 80% first) and fal.ai (prepaid credits, load the smallest top-up or none until A2); name each key bramblewood-local, store as OPENAI_API_KEY / FAL_KEY in your environment, tell me 'keys are set' and I check only that they exist, then run one test through tools/art/pixelize.py. Recommended order: free tiers first (OpenRouter free + Google AI Studio + DeepL API Free + CodeRabbit), routed through LiteLLM or OpenRouter; paid OpenAI / fal keys only when A2 or A3 go ahead. Sources: openrouter.ai/blog/tutorials/free-llm-apis-compared/ ; layer3labs.io/guides/is-gemini-free ; support.deepl.com/hc/en-us/articles/360021200939-DeepL-API-Free ; aicodereview.cc/blog/is-coderabbit-free ; krea.ai/blog/best-free-ai-image-generators-in-2026 ; dupple.com/learn/is-elevenlabs-free ; dupple.com/learn/is-suno-free ; huggingface.co/stabilityai/stable-audio-open-1.0

items.title: Spend about $7-15 to train a Bramblewood pixel LoRA and test it on 10 cards?
items.body: What a Bramblewood pixel LoRA is: a small add-on trained on our own card art so a general image model (FLUX.2 [dev], trained on fal) draws new cards in the same house style; PixelLab stays the main source and heroes stay PixelLab. Data: 20-40 of the best existing PixelLab cards from art/cards (633 PNGs, 256x256 today), picked for one coherent look: same outline weight, same palette (tools/art/palette.json), a spread of subjects (mammal, bird, insect, structure), no text in the image, no watermarked stock. Each image gets a short caption in the style of docs/art-style-prompts.md with a trigger word (for example 'bwpixel') so the style can be called on and off. About half a day of curation, which I can do from the repo; you pick or veto the 30. Tool options: (a) fal's FLUX.2 trainer (hosted, no GPU, upload a zip of images and captions, about 1,000-2,000 steps, roughly $6.40 per 1,000 steps on fal's list, so about $6-13 per training run plus about a few cents per generated image; check the current price on fal's page before any run); (b) Replicate's FLUX trainer (similar, per-run pricing); (c) a local or rented GPU with ai-toolkit/kohya (cheaper per run, but needs a rented GPU and setup time; not worth it for a 10-card test). Recommendation: (a), because A1 already puts a fal key and cap in place. Cost range: a first test is about $7-15 in total (one 1,000-step training plus 10-40 generations), and a retrain with fixes is the same again; a full set of Maps 9-10 cards afterwards is cents per card. All of it stays under the cap you set in A1; nothing runs without your OK on the amount. Test plan on 10 cards: (1) train once on the 30; (2) generate the 10 test cards, chosen from existing cards whose PixelLab art we already like, so each result can be set beside the original (a mix: 3 small animals, 2 birds, 2 insects, 1 structure, 1 large beast, 1 fantasy creature); (3) run each through `tools/art/pixelize.py` (nearest-neighbour downscale to the 160 px grid, palette snap, outline clean-up); (4) review in the hub's Visual Library as 'proposed', scoring each on outline, palette, readable silhouette at card size and fit beside the PixelLab neighbours; (5) pass if at least 7 of 10 are usable with at most a pixel pass and one retry, fail otherwise; (6) if it passes, spend the same amount on the Maps 9-10 cards and the Home sprites that wait on PixelLab; if it fails, delete the LoRA and keep PixelLab only. Needs from you: A1 done, a yes on the training spend, and a veto pass over the 30 picks. | 2026-10-29 (owner 00:10: "Write the chance of this passing, let's say we have 100 artwork we like"): with 100 liked cards as training data (more than the 20-40 planned, so a stronger style signal; about 2,000-3,000 steps, so roughly $13-19 per run at fal's list price, check before any run): my estimate is about 65% that the 10-card test passes (7 or more of the 10 accepted after our usual palette quantise and nearest-neighbour downscale). Style match (palette, outline weight, framing) is the easy part: about 85%. The risk is a true pixel grid: FLUX draws "pixel-look" art with soft, uneven pixels, so each image needs the quantise/downscale clean-up, and roughly 1 in 2 single generations will be usable, so expect 2-3 tries per card. Subjects far from the training set (dinosaurs, golems) fail more often. A 10-card test tells us this for about one run's cost; Claude does not buy the credits.

items.title: Devilry: my readings of your list (all built, all revertible)
items.body: Built as I read them: (1) Dark Summon is a second play each turn, just for ⛧ cards, and every Dark Summon card also costs Darkness (a free extra play measured at 100%). (2) Darkness comes from your own units perishing (+1 each); 'dark actions' were left open. (3) Devour uses your play for the turn and works once per devourer. (4) Ritual's 'units perished' counts both sides. (5) Sacrifice N sits on the fodder; the discount comes off Darkness first, then Lumber. (6) Your blank keyword is named Offering N. 2026-10-10 (you: 'darkness is not clear. Is it gained? idk'): yes, it is gained: +1 each time one of YOUR units perishes (Ash Imp adds +1 on arrival). It's shown only if your deck has at least one Devilry card: the pill reads '★ 3 · ⛧ 1' (Darkness held, dark summons left this turn), and each gain floats a ★ +1. You gain 1 dark summon per turn; it doesn't stack.
items.outcome: Owner (10-23 00:10): "OKAY for now" Keep all six Devilry readings (the default).

But if the enemy has a status that makes them less effective at combat or YOU have a skill that makes you MORE effective at combat (blind vs evade e.g.)" Not the suggestion: Backstab gains its bonus when the target has a status that makes it less effective at combat, or the attacker has a skill that makes it more effective (blind against evade, for example). (F) the same hummingbird nerf, +1 Attack on 6 otter 1-Attack fillers (Honey Bee, Silver Minnow, Duckling, Otter Kit, Worker Ant, Chipmunk Forager), and Reach on Otter Guard and River Carp only: 46.8%. items.title: Cards that cost 3+ Lumber don't pay off
items.body: Cards costing 3+ Lumber (all five dragons included) score ~38% in simulation. 2026-10-09, taking the default on 'continue': all 30 got an arrival effect (dragons breathe 4 on every enemy; brutes hit the enemy opposite for 2× their cost; Elder Willow, Elderhorn Monarch and Riverworks Bastion refund 2 Lumber; the slow small ones delay the enemy opposite by 2 Wait). It didn't move them: the real cause is that Lumber only comes from discarding cards, so a 4-cost card costs five cards in all. Tested a passive income with the CPU saving properly: +1 Lumber every 2 rounds gives cost-2 cards 75%, cost-3+ 51%, dragons 60% (free cards fall to ~24%, as cheap cards should); every round is too much (dragons 96%); every 3 rounds is too little (45%).
options: Keep discard-only Lumber; make big cards cheaper
items.outcome: You chose no free Lumber income (it inflates Lumber costs). Instead, cards that give Lumber or draws (Beaver Lumberjack: +2 Lumber; Courier Pigeon: draw 1), plus a day/night cycle and field cards to make rounds vary. The experimental trickle setting was removed. See fields-and-day-night-2026-10-09.md.
